name: Kebotix, Inc.
subcategory: AI + robotic self-driving lab for materials and chemicals discovery
origin_detail: Cambridge, MA company (501 Massachusetts Ave.) offering an AI platform and closed-loop 'predict-produce-prove' self-driving lab for materials and chemicals. Investors shown on its site: Embark Ventures, One Way Ventures, Taihill Venture, Flybridge, WorldQuant Ventures, ArcTern Ventures, Novo Holdings, Baidu Ventures, SIT Capital, Propagator Ventures. A Harvard spin-out origin and founders are not confirmed in fetched sources; CEO Jill Becker and CSO Semion Saikin are named in a news headline.
openness_notes: No open-source code, data, models or hardware designs found on kebotix.com. The platform and lab are proprietary.
risk_events: 2019-2020 recognition: C&EN Top 10 chemistry start-ups to watch (2019), WEF Technology Pioneer (2020), MIT Technology Review 'AI-discovered molecules' key player

Partnerships listed: Bayer, bp, Johnson Matthey, Mitsubishi Chemical, Valqua (3-year deal, ~Mar 2022), University of Toronto (OLEDs), SCM, Northeastern Roux Institute; EPA safe-pigments project; industry partner in a $15M NSF institute
Dormancy signal: the news page's latest dated item is ~Mar 2022 (Valqua); only the footer shows (c) 2026, and no later news, funding or hiring evidence was found
robustness: Unclear and likely weak. A small VC-backed proprietary platform with no visible activity since 2022, and nothing open that could outlive it. Whether it shut down, was acquired or is dormant could not be determined without web search.
physical_science_relevance: Very high. It was one of the first commercial 'self-driving labs' for materials and chemicals, working on OLED materials, safe pigments (EPA), crop protection (Bayer), toxicity (Mitsubishi Chemical) and digital materials strategy (Johnson Matthey, bp).
openness_effect_assessment: Kebotix commercialized the self-driving-lab concept as a closed platform and partnership business. It released nothing open, so its methods left no public trace for the SDL community to build on. Its apparent stall after 2022, before the 2025 AI-for-science funding boom, suggests the closed model did not by itself secure capital or survival for an early mover.
key_takeaway: Kebotix was an early (c. 2017-2022) closed AI-plus-robotics materials-discovery startup with strong recognition (C&EN, WEF, MIT Tech Review) and blue-chip partners, but its public activity stops around 2022. Whether it 'shut down' is unconfirmed: the website is live with a 2026 copyright but has no news after ~Mar 2022. It is a cautionary early mover that predates the 2025-2026 funding wave and left no open artifacts.
notes: No WebSearch queries were run for this organization (shared WebSearch budget exhausted); facts come from kebotix.com pages listed in fetched_urls.

unconfirmed.reason: Left null. No official page states current status, and kebotix.com shows only a (c) 2026 footer. The latest primary evidence of activity is from 2024. Ashland's 8 May 2024 release (8-K EX-99.1) says 'Kulkarni is the CEO of Kebotix, a startup company focused on commercializing artificial intelligence methods'. Kebotix's own Form D signed 2024-08-05 shows an equity first sale 2024-07-22, $4,999,765 sold of $9,999,999. A ConnectM 8-K exhibit (19 Oct 2026) lists 'Chief Executive Officer of Kebotix' among Ashish Kulkarni's executive roles, without saying whether the role is current. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kebotix returns 404. Nothing states 2026 status.

Left null because no page states a total. SEC Form D equity sales: 2018 (first sale 2018-07-23) $5,055,279; 2020 (2020-04-02) $11,388,778 of $15M; 2023 (2023-03-29) $2,209,999 of $3,999,999; 2024 (2024-07-22) $4,999,765 of $9,999,999. That sums to $23,653,821 (my arithmetic; Reg D sales only). These are not filled.

verification_pass2.note: risk_events[2] ('no later news, funding or hiring evidence') and robustness ('no visible activity since 2022') are contradicted by Kebotix's own SEC Form Ds: equity sales in Mar 2023 and Jul 2024. The 2018 Form D lists Jill Becker (executive officer, director, promoter), Alan Aspuru-Guzik (director, promoter) and Semyon Dukach (director), which bears on the unconfirmed founders/origin. By the 2023 Form D, Ashish Kulkarni was executive officer and director, Becker was no longer listed, and Aspuru-Guzik, Semion Saykin and Dennis Sheberla were executive officers. Form Ds show a Delaware, privately funded company (ownership_status null not changed). Wikipedia (Alan Aspuru-Guzik) says 'He is the co-founder of Kebotix', which supports the founders' identity left unconfirmed in origin_detail. The earliest Form D gives the Cambridge address as 23 Perry Street, so the 501 Massachusetts Ave address is the later one.
